At the origin the multiplicities are 2,2,3,4,5 with lowest nonzero homogeneous parts y^2, -y^2, y(3x^2-y^2), -4x^2y^2 and -y^3(x^2+y^2); the scheme-theoretic tangent cones are Spec(k[x,y]/(y^2)) for both X_1 and X_2, Spec(k[x,y]/(y(3x^2-y^2))), Spec(k[x,y]/(x^2y^2)) and Spec(k[x,y]/(y^3(x^2+y^2))); every tangent space is k^2 of dimension two; and the cone equations factor over k as y*y, y(sqrt3 x-y)(sqrt3 x+y), x*x*y*y and y*y*y(x+iy)(x-iy) whose distinct factors are pairwise non-proportional, so these cones are a doubled line, three distinct lines, the two coordinate axes each doubled, and a tripled line together with two distinct further lines. The first two equations define different closed subschemes of A^2_k although their multiplicity, tangent cone and tangent space all agree.
items.strategy: Expand each equation, read off the lowest nonzero homogeneous part and its degree, apply the initial-ideal presentation of the tangent cone, factor the cone generator over the algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 into linear forms, test pairwise non-proportionality of the distinct factors by coefficients, and evaluate the Jacobian at the origin. The computation verifies the shared data only and does not classify analytic branches as tacnodes or ramphoid cusps.

items.title: Classical bilinear-form equations linearize to matrix spaces
items.statement: Let k be a field and n≥1. If char(k)≠2, define O_n and SO_n as the affine k-schemes cut out in M_n by A^tA=I_n and by A^tA=I_n, det(A)=1, respectively; at I_n their tangent spaces are the skew-symmetric matrices. In every characteristic, for J=[[0,I_n],[-I_n,0]], define Sp_n in M_{2n} by A^tJA=J and det(A)=1. At I_{2n}, its tangent matrices are [[P,Q],[R,-P^t]] with Q,R symmetric, and this tangent vector space has dimension n(2n+1). These computations make no claim about global group-scheme dimension or smoothness.

references.title: Example 4.48, Exercise 4-6, and official solution 4-6, printed pp.97–99 and p.222

items.strategy: Use based dual-number maps into the equation-defined affine schemes, writing A=I+epsilon B. For the orthogonal equation obtain B^t+B=0; in characteristic not two this also forces trace B=0, so the SO determinant equation adds no linear condition. For the standard alternating block J solve B^t J+JB=0; this gives B=[[P,Q],[R,-P^t]] with Q,R symmetric and forces trace B=0 in every characteristic, so det A=1 adds no linear condition. Count the independent entries. State tangent-vector dimensions only; do not infer global group-scheme dimension or smoothness.

items.title: An irreducible curve can have arbitrarily large tangent dimension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field, let n>=1, and let C=Spec(k[t^n,t^{n+1},...,t^{2n-1}]) be the monomial curve carried by the subring R=k[t^n,...,t^{2n-1}] of k[t]. Its maximal ideal m=(t^n,...,t^{2n-1})R has residue field R/m=k, so the origin m is a k-rational point; the classes of t^n,...,t^{2n-1} form a k-basis of m/m^2, so dim_k T_0C=n; and R is a domain with dim R=1, so C is an irreducible curve. There is no closed immersion C -> A^{n-1}_k of k-schemes. Hence for every n>=1 there is an irreducible curve whose tangent space at a point has dimension n, and it cannot be embedded in A^{n-1}_k.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, v6.10, Exercise 4-5 (printed p. 99) with its solution (printed p. 223)

items.strategy: Construct R as the image of k[x_n,...,x_{2n-1}] in k[t]; it is a domain. The element t is integral over R, so the AC-carrying integral-extension dimension theorem gives dim R=1. At the rational origin m=(t^n,...,t^{2n-1}), the n monomials of degrees n through 2n-1 form a basis of m/m^2, hence dim T_0C=n. A hypothetical closed immersion into A^{n-1}_k has a surjective map on local rings at 0 by the published definition; it therefore surjects on cotangent spaces and injects T_0C into T_p A^{n-1}_k=k^{n-1}, contradicting dimensions. AC is used through the integral-extension dimension and irreducibility suppliers; the tangent obstruction is direct and requires no affine quotient classification.

items.title: A nonradical ideal need not enlarge every tangent space
items.statement: In k[x,y], I=(x^2,xy) is strictly smaller than its radical (x). At the k-rational point (0,1) the closed subscheme Spec(k[x,y]/I) and the reduced line Spec(k[x,y]/(x)) have the same one-dimensional tangent space inside k^2, because y is a unit in the local ring there and I agrees with (x) after localisation. At the origin the tangent space of Spec(k[x,y]/I) is all of k^2 (dimension two), while the reduced line has tangent space of dimension one. A nonradical ideal therefore need not enlarge the tangent space at every point; the witness works over any field and in every characteristic.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, v6.10, Exercise 4-9 (printed p.99) and its official solution (printed p.223)

items.strategy: Recompute the radical choice-free: ker(ev) = (x) for the map ev: k[x][y] -> k[y] with x -> 0, y -> y, obtained from the coefficient expression in the iterated ring and division by the monic polynomial x; k[y] a domain gives sqrt(I) = (x). Then compute the Jacobian rows (2x,0) and (y,x) at (0,1) and at the origin, compare with the row (1,0) for (x), and explain the equality at (0,1) by y being a unit in the local ring R_(x,y-1), where I and (x) agree after localisation. This answers Exercise 4-9 in every characteristic without AC.
